segments.t: Attio MCP connects external AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to your Attio workspace, so you can search your CRM, update records, log notes, and manage tasks in natural language from wherever you already work with AI. This guide covers connecting Attio to your AI assistant, verifying the connection, and a library of role-based prompts for getting real work done, whether you run the whole company, RevOps, or your own book of business.

(Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants securely interact with other systems. Your AI assistant connects to Attio's MCP server, you sign in with your Attio account, and the assistant can then use a set of Attio tools: searching records, creating and updating records, working with notes and tasks, managing views, and reading emails and meeting data.
full list of the Attio MCP’s tools
Three things are worth understanding before you connect:
The AI assistant authenticates as your Attio user through OAuth. It can only see and change what your own permissions allow.
You control what runs without asking.

By default, your AI assistant asks for your approval before running most Attio tools. In your assistant's settings, you can allow specific tools, like read tools that search and view data, to run without asking. If you're in a managed workspace on your AI assistant, the available options may be restricted, e.g. write tools can’t be set to
It works alongside Ask Attio, not instead of it.
Ask Attio is AI inside Attio and needs no setup. MCP is for working outside Attio, where you can combine your CRM with other tools and data the assistant can reach. Learn more about
when to use Attio MCP or Ask Attio
You need an Attio account on any plan. All workspace members can use the MCP.

You need an AI assistant that supports MCP connections, such as Claude or ChatGPT. Whether connectors are available can depend on your plan with that assistant, and if your AI assistant is managed by an admin, you may need them to enable the Attio connector.
Know which workspace you want to connect. If you belong to more than one Attio workspace, you choose one during sign-in.
Claude and ChatGPT connect through their built-in connector directories, and any other MCP-compatible assistant connects using the server URL
setup steps for your assistant in the Attio MCP developer documentation
, signing in with your Attio account when prompted.

Find the company record for [a domain you know is in your CRM, e.g. attio.com] and summarize what we know.

lines.t: The prompts that survive daily use are worth standardizing. Write the best ones into a shared doc, or save them as reusable prompts or skills in your AI assistant, so every rep runs the same reliable version instead of improvising.

segments.t: Here are a few prompting habits to help you get the best results from the Attio MCP:
Use a full name plus company, or better, a unique value like an email address or domain.
"Create a deal for Brightline" is clearer than "add Brightline," which could mean a company, a person, or a list entry.
Use attribute names as they appear in Attio.
If you're unsure, ask the assistant to list an object's attributes first, then reference the exact names and options.
Include a unique value when creating records.

Provide an email address for person records or a domain for company records. Attio deduplicates automatically when a unique value is provided, so Attio can update existing records or create them if they don’t exist.
End write requests with "list everything you changed, with links to the records." Then spot-check the record in Attio while you're learning which phrasings work reliably.
The assistant says it can't see a record you know exists:

Your Attio permissions apply to the connection too. Read access to objects and records can't be restricted per member, but list access can be. If a list is restricted for you, the assistant can't see its entries either.
Changes appear in the wrong workspace:
The connection was authorized against a different workspace. Disconnect the Attio connector in your AI assistant, reconnect, and choose the correct workspace during sign-in.
Duplicate records after the assistant creates:
Creation prompts without a unique value can produce duplicates. Include an email address for people or a domain for companies, and Attio matches to the existing record automatically.
Requests start failing after heavy use:
per workspace. Ask the assistant to slow down or run operations one at a time, then retry. Normal conversational use stays well within limits.

segments.t: Calculating Deal value from the products or services on each deal gives every rep the same structure to work in, and gives your reports and forecasts consistent numbers. This article shows you how to set up two custom objects, three formulas, and three workflows that calculate Deal value for you. When a rep adds line items to a deal, Attio totals them and updates the Deal value. Each product's price is locked in on the line item when it's created, so changing a product's price later never rewrites past deals. Deals without line items keep the value reps type in.
If you haven't created custom objects or workflows before, read
first. This article focuses on what to build and why.

blocks.text: Decide whether you need products and line items

segments.t: This setup is worth it when your team sells more than one product or variable quantities of a product on the same deal. A deal for 40 seats of a license plus an implementation fee is a good example.
If every deal is for one product at one price, you don't need to add complexity through this setup. A typed Deal value or a single formula attribute on Deals is enough.
The tradeoff is setup time, but once it's built, Deal value maintains itself.

blocks.text: Check that prices stay locked and Deal value syncs

segments.t: Run three quick checks on your test deal:
Change List price on a test product. Line items that already use it keep their Locked price, and Deal value doesn't change. If Lumora raised Platform license to $700, Ridgeway's line would keep $600.

blocks.text: Use Deal value in reports and forecasts

segments.t: With Deal value calculated from line items, every report, view, and forecast that uses it is built on consistent numbers. The natural next step is to weight Deal value by stage probability. Learn how in

faq.q: Why is Locked price empty on some line items?

segments.t: Line items created before the first workflow existed won't have a Locked price. To fill it in, clear the line item's

, then select the product again. This triggers the workflow, which copies the product's current List price. If the product's price has changed since the deal was made, check that Locked price matches what was sold.

faq.q: Can I edit line items on a closed deal?

segments.t: Yes, and Line items total updates, but Deal value doesn't. That keeps closed deals at the value they closed at. If the change should count, update Deal value by hand.

faq.q: Can I stop reps from changing line items or products on a deal?

segments.t: No, anyone with access to edit line items can change them. If a rep types over Deal value on an open deal with line items, the third workflow changes it back. See the section on stopping reps from typing over Deal value.

faq.q: Does this work with more than one currency?

segments.t: Each currency attribute uses one currency, set in its attribute settings, so every line item and deal in this setup shares the same currency. Formulas don't convert between currencies, so set List price, Locked price, Line items total, and Deal value to the same one. Otherwise, the number carries over unchanged. For example, a €5,000 Locked price becomes $5,000 in a Line items total set to US dollars.

faq.q: Why do my existing Deal value automations run more often after this setup?

segments.t: Deal value updates every time a line item changes. Workflows or alerts that trigger on Deal value changes run each time, and they can run on a value partway through a rep's edits. Consider triggering them on a stage change instead, or adding a condition such as a minimum value.

segments.t: Multiple pipelines let you manage different deal flows and sales motions separately in Attio. For example, as a software business, you may sell multiple different products or want one pipeline for new business and one for renewals and expansions. As a
, you may want one pipeline for sourcing and evaluating investment opportunities and one for managing LP relationships and fundraising rounds.
Attio supports two approaches to managing multiple pipelines, and there are some factors to consider when choosing the right one for your business.
Before setting up your pipelines, consider the following:
How similar are your pipelines? Are they related or separate processes? Think about the attributes and stages each pipeline requires.
What objects are associated with each pipeline? For example, one pipeline might relate to the standard Companies object while another relates to the standard People object.
Do you want all pipelines in one report, or should they be separate? Attio’s reporting tool supports one data source per report, which affects the approach you choose.

blocks.text: Option 1: Use the Deals object with a select attribute to separate pipelines

segments.t: This works best when your pipelines share the same stages and attributes, and you want to report on them together. Each pipeline becomes a filtered view of the Deals object, so you don't duplicate your data model. In the table below, you’ll see examples of when this is a good approach.

rows: Separate sales teams handle small and large customers.
The Sales team close new business while Success own renewals and expansion.
Each region wants their own view to run their sales process.

segments.t: Learn how to set up the Deals object with a select attribute to separate pipelines.

blocks.text: Option 2: Use separate objects when pipelines differ

segments.t: This works best when pipelines differ significantly in data, stages, or associated objects. Each pipeline lives in its own object, so reports on these pipelines stay separate and can’t be combined.

Software deals go through a demo and trial, services deals need scoping and a statement of work, and a different team often sells each.

segments.t: Use this guide to set a workspace-wide privacy baseline before inviting members, then help each member finish their mailbox settings after syncing. You’ll decide which communications stay private, which should never appear in Attio, and how much email context teammates can see.
This guide gives recommendations on how to configure three visibility features:
Admin-managed rules that apply across every synced mailbox. Use
to hide internal emails and calendar events, and
when that communication must stay out of Attio entirely. Later in this guide, we’ll share more detail on how to decide what to protect or block. See
Keep emails and calendar events private
for more detail and setup steps.

blocks.text: Configure workspace settings before inviting members

segments.t: Admins should set workspace settings before inviting members so the privacy baseline is in place before anyone connects a mailbox.
On all plans, Attio adds workspace-member email addresses and domains to the
list as Protected, but admins can turn off that protection.

Domains are those associated with an email address in the workspace. For example, if you have jamie@basepoint.com and alex@basepoint.io in the workspace, basepoint.com and basepoint.io are your workspace-member domains. Public email domains such as gmail.com are not treated as workspace-member domains.
Workspace-member email addresses and domains include active and suspended members, pending invitees, and connected mailboxes. These addresses are always Protected.
To ensure domain protection is enabled, navigate to the
, check that toggles for internal domains are enabled.

External collaborators are companies and people outside of your business who are not users of your Attio workspace, but whose communication could be considered private. This might include sensitive vendors, contractors, law firms or investors.
list, choose a setting based on where the collaborator’s communication should remain visible.

Choose this option when you want the collaborator’s communication history on their record. For example, you might leave a video editor unprotected so their person record shows emails with your team. We recommend leaving customer communication unprotected because your CRM should be the home for all of your contact history with customers and prospects.

Use this when the collaborator’s records should remain private, but their customer-facing communication may still be useful. For example, protect a fractional legal firm’s domain so email exclusively between employees and the firm is hidden from Attio, but communication also including third parties, like a customer, is still visible on those third party’s record pages.
Use this when no communication involving the collaborator or firm should appear anywhere. For example, blocking a payroll provider also hides its emails from other participants’ records.
Protect an individual email address when the rule applies only to that person. Protect a domain when the company record and everyone using that domain should be protected.

blocks.text: Block contacts that must stay out

segments.t: , add contacts whose communication should never enter Attio to the

list and set their enforcement level to Blocked. Common examples include a payroll provider, a personal correspondent, or an external adviser handling matters that must never be visible in the workspace.
Do not block public email domains such as gmail.com. Doing so will hide all email with anyone who uses that provider, including customers and prospects.

Blocking is intentionally broad. If a Blocked accountant or law firm is copied on an email about a customer contract, Attio also hides the thread on the customer’s record. Use Protected instead when the adviser’s records should remain private but your team still needs customer-facing threads elsewhere in Attio.
Investor domains need a deliberate choice because the right setting depends on how your team uses Attio.
Leave investor domains unprotected when investors are part of the pipeline, such as at a venture capital firm. Control who can read the email body through sharing settings instead.

: Set investor domains to Protected when you don’t want communications between your company and the investment firm to show in Attio, but you want to see communications involving your investor and third parties, like introductions to other people or businesses.

Set investor domains to Blocked when a founder wants all fundraising correspondence hidden from the team. The tradeoff is that investor introductions and other customer communication including investors will also be hidden from Attio.

blocks.text: Set an email visibility policy for your team

segments.t: Decide how much of each member’s synced email should be visible to the rest of the workspace. This setting is managed individually by each member for their own mailbox and cannot be set by admins, so agree on a policy for your team and ask members to apply it when they connect their mailboxes.

If teammates regularly need to read each other’s email threads, consider
to give specific people access rather than sharing email bodies with everyone.

After this phase, internal protection is either enabled or deliberately disabled, parties that should never appear in Attio are blocked, you have decided how to handle investors, and your team has agreed which sharing level members should apply to their mailboxes.
Each member should review two mailbox settings once their mailbox has synced. Admins cannot configure these settings on their behalf.

If your work mailbox may carry some correspondence that isn't company business, you can add those people to your mailbox-only blocklist to keep those emails and calendar events private, along with your own personal email address.
A mailbox-only blocklist applies only to emails and calendar events synced from that mailbox, so another member can still sync their own copy of a thread or event with the same person.

For example, if you add your personal Gmail address to your mailbox-only blocklist, emails between that address and your work mailbox won't show in Attio. Neither will a personal calendar invite you send from your Gmail to your work address to block out time. However, if you email your work address and CC a colleague's work address, that email shows in Attio if your colleague has their mailbox synced.
Review the sharing level for your mailbox and apply the policy your team agreed on.

This approach gives the operating team the context it needs without sharing every mailbox with the whole workspace.
After this phase, each member should have a mailbox-only blocklist and a sharing level they have reviewed.

When account coverage changes, remove individual full access that is no longer needed.

segments.t: A weighted pipeline adjusts each deal's value by its likelihood of closing, giving you a more accurate forecast than raw pipeline totals. For example, a $50,000 deal with a 40% close probability contributes $20,000 to your weighted pipeline. This guide walks through the full setup: a formula attribute that calculates each deal's weighted value from its deal stage, and the reports that turn weighted values into a forecast.

blocks.text: How a weighted pipeline works in Attio

segments.t: The weighted value is calculated by a single formula attribute. The formula reads each deal's stage, matches it to a close probability you define, and multiplies the Deal value by that probability.

Once this formula is created, weighted values appear for every deal that have a Deal value, including deals already in your pipeline. When a deal is created or moves to a new stage, its weighted value recalculates automatically.

A deal can only be in one stage at a time, so the conditions add up to a single probability. The formula multiplies the deal value by that probability and divides by 100 to express it as a percentage.

faq.q: Do I need to update my existing deals?

segments.t: No. The formula calculates from each deal's current stage, so every deal with a deal value shows a weighted value as soon as you save the formula.

faq.q: What happens to deals in a stage that isn't in the formula?

segments.t: They get a weighted value of zero. This is useful for lost stages, but it also means new pipeline stages won't count toward your weighted pipeline until you add them to the formula.

faq.q: How do I add a new deal stage to the formula?

segments.t: Create the weighted value formula attribute
to edit the attribute. Then, use the AI composer with the following prompt:
Add a new deal stage. It's called [DEAL STAGE] and I want the probability to be [PROBABILITY].

faq.q: How do I change the probability for a stage?

segments.t: Open the Weighted value attribute, edit the probability in the relevant
condition, and save. All deals recalculate automatically.

faq.q: What if I add or rename a pipeline stage?

segments.t: Renaming an existing deal stage doesn't affect the formula, so deals in that stage will still show a weighted value.
However, if you add a new deal stage, update the formula to match. Deals in the newly-created stage will not show a weighted value until that stage is added to the formula with a probability value.

faq.q: Why isn't my deal showing a weighted value?

segments.t: Check that the deal has a value in the Deal value attribute. The formula multiplies the deal value, so deals without one won't show a weighted value.
Also, check which stage the deal is in, and make sure that stage is in the formula.

To update existing records with a CSV import in Attio, you need to use a unique attribute that helps identify each record. Without a unique attribute, Attio will create duplicate records instead of updating existing ones.
Some attributes in Attio are designated as “unique”. When an attribute is unique, it means no two records can share the same value for that attribute.
For example, Domains and Email addresses are unique attributes:
can have the same name but must have unique domains.
can share names but must have unique email addresses.

lines.t: It’s usually simpler to update records with a unique attribute like Email or Domain, rather than using Record ID. However, you’ll need to use Record ID if there isn’t another unique attribute available or when you don’t have values for the other unique attributes (for example, if you need to update a company with an import but it has no domain). Learn more about using Record IDs below.

blocks.text: When to use Record ID and Entry ID

segments.t: Record ID is a unique attribute on all objects, and Entry ID is unique on all list entries in Attio. You can’t add or change these IDs, and they are generated by Attio upon creation. But when all records or entries you want to import already exist in Attio, you can use the IDs assigned by Attio to locate and update the existing records.

lines.t: Do not include Record ID in your file if you’re adding any new records, as they won’t import successfully. If you’re using Record ID to make updates and your file has a mix of existing and new records, split them into separate files, or use another unique attribute like Domains or Email addresses, which works for both existing and new records.

This is separate from the duplicate records described below, which happen when a unique attribute isn't mapped at all.
CSV imports can create two types of duplicates:

segments.t: Attio includes an optional setting that protects against formula injection in CSV exports. It's available to workspace admins on all plans, and is disabled by default.

Formula injection occurs when data containing spreadsheet formulas has been entered into a text attribute. When exported and opened in Excel or a similar application, those formulas may execute automatically. When this setting is enabled, Attio adds a prefix to text field values to prevent that from happening.

Turn it on only if your security team has identified formula injection as a risk. Enabling it changes the format of text field values in exported files, which could affect downstream processes that rely on those exports.

faq.q: Can I migrate notes with Import2, but not records?

segments.t: This is possible, but you will need to reach out to the Import2 team at
(cc support@attio.com) to configure this for you.

faq.q: What happens to records that already exist when I run the migration?

segments.t: Import2 checks for existing records using email addresses for people and domains for companies. If they already exist, attributes on the existing records are not updated, but any notes and tasks from your former CRM are added.

faq.q: Can I restart or undo a migration?

segments.t: Yes. Import2 provides options for both redoing and reverting migrations:
– Use this if you need to run the import again with corrections or updates.
– This removes the records that were added during the migration.

Undoing a migration only removes imported records. It does not remove lists, attributes, or other structures created during the process. If you need a complete reset to factory settings, contact Import2 directly at

faq.q: Can I choose which data to import?

segments.t: By default, all supported standard objects are enabled, and you can select any custom objects you want to migrate in Settings when you initiate your sample import. You can
configure which objects you want to migrate
both during the sample setup and after the sample is complete if you want to make changes.

faq.q: Will Import2 automatically link people to their companies?

segments.t: If they were associated in your previous CRM, then the companies and people will also be associated in Attio, even if the person's email domain and company domain don't match. A person linked to a company in Attio will show on the company's Team attribute, and the company will show on the person's Company attribute.

faq.q: Can I migrate custom objects?

segments.t: Yes, you can select the custom objects in the Settings when you initiate your sample import. If a custom object already exists in Attio, Import2 will find it by name and import the data into it. If it does not exist yet, Import2 will create the custom object and its fields within Attio and import into the newly created custom object. The mappings for the custom object attributes will appear in the mapping step along with other objects where you can adjust them if needed.

faq.q: My team is already up and running in Attio and I don't want to delete records or remove email sync prior to migrating. What should I do?

segments.t: If it’s not possible for you to remove synced accounts and delete records, you can go ahead and perform the Import2 migration, keeping in mind that if a person or company record already exists in Attio its attribute values won’t be updated from your former CRM. To update those separately, export your companies and people records from your former CRM, and
import them to Attio via CSV

segments.t: Attributes are customizable fields that store information about your records in Attio. They help you capture and organize important data points such as a person’s location, their company, or the date of your last email interaction.
Attributes are useful for filtering, sorting, and segmenting your records to fit your workflow. Each column in the below table view is an attribute: Domains, Description, and Categories.

lines.t: This article focuses on attributes for objects and lists, but attributes can also be added to activities and activity schemas. Learn more in
Create and manage activities and schemas

segments.t: Each object in Attio, such as People, Companies, or Deals, includes a set of system attributes. These are built-in fields automatically created by Attio. While system attributes cannot be deleted or archived, you can
customize which attributes are shown on record pages
. For a complete list of system attributes available for standard objects, see
In addition to system attributes, you can
to store any additional data specific to your needs.

Companies and people records have a set of system enriched attributes that auto-populate based on data sourced about your records. In addition, Attio populates communication intelligence attributes using data from
Enriched values have a purple background, and enriched attributes show a sparkle icon next to their name in table views.
You can create custom attributes on any object in Attio to capture information that isn't covered by the built-in system attributes.

blocks.text: Choose between an object and list attribute

segments.t: Before creating a new attribute, decide whether it should be an

Object attributes apply to every record of a specific object type (e.g., all companies or all people) across your workspace. They can be displayed in any list or all records view for the object within your workspace. For example, a "Domains" attribute for the company object will be visible on all company records and can be used in any view of companies.
Only admins and members with Full access to the object can create or modify object attributes, but all team members with
can assign values to them. Object attributes are managed in
List attributes are specific to a single list and cannot be used outside of it. Use list attributes for details that are only relevant to one list, such as "Owner," "Priority," or "Stage."
Only admins and members with Full access to the list can create or modify list attributes, but all team members with
can assign values to them. List attributes are managed in
if it applies to all records of a certain object type across your workspace or is relevant in multiple lists.
if it is specific to a single list or subset of records.

On lists, custom objects, and the Deals, Workspaces and Users objects, you can set a default value for an attribute so that each new record or list entry is automatically pre-filled with that value. Default values cannot be set for attributes on the People and Companies objects.

, you can define a set of options that appear in a dropdown. This lets users choose from preset values instead of typing them manually, similar to a multiple choice field in a form. There is a limit of 5,000 options per attribute.

lines.t: Deleting an option will also remove any existing data that uses it. This cannot be undone.

segments.t: Some Attio objects support creating custom required and unique attributes. Standard objects also have system unique and required attributes, which you can learn about in
A required attribute must be filled out when a new record is created.
Custom required attributes can only be created on

Rules let you require attribute values under specific conditions. Unlike required attributes, rules can be created on any object, including standard objects. Learn more about
A unique attribute ensures that no two records can share the same value, which helps prevent duplicate records.
Custom unique attributes can be created on

lines.t: Unique attributes treat letter casing as different values. For example, “Value” and “value” would be accepted as unique.

faq.q: Does restoring an attribute also restore attribute values? Can attributes be restored indefinitely?

segments.t: Yes, when you restore an attribute, its values will also be restored and can be utilized in reports, but the attribute will not automatically be re-added to be displayed in your views. You will need to
Archived attributes can be restored at any time, indefinitely.

faq.q: What happens if an enriched attribute value is manually edited?

segments.t: Any manually entered data in enriched attributes will not be overwritten, so the attribute will not be enriched in the future unless the manually entered data is removed.

faq.q: Can I set a default currency? How do I change an attribute's currency?

segments.t: Currency is set individually per attribute, and each attribute can use a single currency. There is not currently a way to set a default currency.

segments.t: with copy and paste in table views, or by using our importer to make bulk updates. See the linked articles for details.

faq.q: What format is required for the phone number attribute?

segments.t: When adding a phone number to Attio, it needs to follow a specific international format called E.164. This means the number should start with a
, including the area code: ([+][country code][subscriber number including area code])

Attio also checks to make sure the number is likely to be real. It verifies things like valid area codes and whether the number follows the rules for that country. So if you try to add a fake or incorrectly formatted number, it might return an error and fail to save or import.

faq.q: Can I add email addresses to company records?

segments.t: If you just want to add an email address for a company in order to track that information, you can create an object attribute for "Email" and this will allow you to save email addresses for companies. ⁠ ⁠However, it's not possible currently to initiate sending an email to a company record. ⁠⁠So you may want to

for any email addresses associated with the company. They'll automatically be linked to the company if their email domain matches the company's domain, and then any email correspondence you have with them will show on the company "Emails" tab. This also allows you to
to those email addresses within Attio.

faq.q: What are the differences between status and select attribute types?

segments.t: are designed to track which stage each record is currently in within a process or pipeline. They're required for
where each status becomes a column, allowing you to visualize records as cards moving through different stages.

are general-purpose dropdown fields that let you pick from color-coded options to categorize your data. They're perfect for any type of classification that doesn't represent stages of a process or pipeline.
type attribute for tracking deal stages like "Prospecting," "Meeting," or "Proposal" in a pipeline. You'd use a
attribute for categorizing companies by industry, size, or customer segment.
Both allow you to define custom options, but
attributes are specifically optimized for pipeline or process management and kanban board functionality.

segments.t: Each example gives you a prompt to paste into the AI composer, which appears when you create or edit a formula attribute.
The composer builds the formula for you, referencing the actual attributes in your workspace, so you don't need to fix attribute references by hand or learn the formula syntax first.
Create a formula attribute on the object we recommend for that formula.
Paste the prompt into the composer.
Adjust the parts in [square brackets] to match your attribute names and values.

Some examples reference custom attributes, such as a contract start date or a discount percentage, that may not exist in your workspace yet. Where that's the case, we call it out so you can create and populate the attribute before building the formula. The composer can only reference attributes that already exist.
A weighted pipeline adjusts each deal's value by its likelihood of closing, giving you a more accurate forecast than raw pipeline totals.
For example, a $50,000 deal with a 40% close probability contributes $20,000 to your weighted pipeline.
The formula that calculates this weighted deal value will be unique to you as it will contain your own deal stages, and the probabilities you set for each stage.
A count formula tells you how many records are linked to the current record through a relationship attribute, giving you a number you can filter, sort, and report on.
You can build this on any object with a relationship attribute that links more than one record.
This formula is quicker to build by hand than with the AI composer, so we'll build this directly in the formula editor.

A lead score combines multiple signals into a single priority number. Where you store the score depends on your sales motion: outbound teams typically score Companies or People based on ICP fit and intent signals, while inbound teams usually score the record that captures the inbound event, typically a Deal.

Lead scoring only works if you're already capturing the signals you want to score. Effective models combine two dimensions: fit (would this be a good customer?) and intent (are they showing buying signals?). Use fit to qualify and intent to prioritize. Some signals are populated by Attio automatically, while others come from your own tools and processes:

Marketing attribution, such as UTM parameters captured at signup
Your product database or analytics tool, synced via the API
Data providers and visitor deanonymization tools

faq.q: Why is my formula showing the wrong currency?

segments.t: Formulas don't convert between currencies. If the output currency doesn't match the currency of your input attributes, the number is relabeled, not converted. For example, a $1,000 deal at 50% probability shows as £500 if the output currency is set to GBP. Set the output currency to match your input attributes.

faq.q: What happens to my formula attributes if I downgrade to Free or Plus?

segments.t: If your workspace downgrades to the Free or Plus plan, existing formula attributes will stop recalculating and their values will be frozen. Formula attributes will not be visible in table views until the workspace upgrades to the Pro or Ultra plan.

faq.q: Can I write custom code or JavaScript in a formula?

segments.t: No. Formula attributes use Attio's formula language, which includes a defined set of functions and operators. Custom code execution is not supported.

faq.q: Do formula attributes use workspace credits?

segments.t: No. Formula attributes do not require workspace credits, including use of the AI composer.

faq.q: If I rename an attribute option, will my formula still work?

segments.t: It depends on how you referenced the option. If you selected the option from the suggestions in the formula editor, the formula links to the option itself and continues to work after a rename. If you typed the option as text in quotes, it is treated as a fixed string and will not update if the option is renamed.

segments.t: Relationship attributes in Attio let you show how records are connected. They’re useful for mapping real-world relationships, like which people work at a company, which deals are linked to which companies, or how custom objects relate to each other.

These attributes are not just for linking records. Once records are connected, you can display, filter, and sort by attributes from the linked records in any view. This gives you more context and flexibility when working with your data.

Relationship attributes, sometimes called lookup fields in other tools, link records to each other. A relationship attribute consists of two attributes: one on each side of the relationship. When you add Record A to a relationship attribute on Record B, Record B is automatically added to the corresponding attribute on Record A.
For example, below when Prismex is added as Caleb’s Company, Caleb is automatically added to the Team for Prismex.
With custom relationship attributes, you can:
Connect records from two different objects (more common), or records from the same object.
Allow one or multiple records to be linked on each side of the relationship.

The value of relationship attributes in Attio goes beyond simply linking two records. They also give you access to the full set of attributes on the connected record. For example, when a company is linked added to a person via a relationship, you can also display any attribute on the company in views of people.
Attio has multiple system relationship attributes that connect records in your workspace. These system relationship attributes are available by default on all Attio plans, and they cannot be edited.
Associated deals <> Associated company - Many to one
Associated deals <> Associated people - Many to many
Associated users <> Person - Many to one
To represent custom relationships between records in your workspace, you can create your own relationship attributes.
Relationship attributes can only be created on objects only, not on lists.
You must be a workspace admin or have Full access to objects on both side of the relationship to create relationship attributes.
Creating custom relationship attributes is available on Pro, Enterprise, and Ultra plans.

The value of relationship attributes in Attio goes beyond simply linking two records. They also give you access to the full set of attributes on the connected record. For example, if you’ve linked Deals and Companies, you can display, filter, or sort by any company attribute in a view of Deals, and the same applies in reverse.
To display, filter, or sort by an attribute from a linked record:

There are a few important behaviors to be aware of when working with relationships that support multiple values (for example, one to many or many to many relationships).

blocks.text: Path limits when using multi-value relationships

segments.t: When referencing attributes through relationships, only one multi-value relationship can be used in a single attribute path. If a path includes more than one, the system won’t be able to retrieve the data.
Let’s say you have this structure:
A company is linked to multiple people
Each person is linked to multiple projects (a custom object)
In this setup, if you're building a view of companies:
show all the people linked to each companies

That’s because the path from Company → People → Projects involves two multi-value relationships.
When you filter using an attribute from a multi-value relationship, the filter checks for
For example, in a view of companies:
Team > Primary location > City is London

If Team or an attribute on people is displayed in the view, this filter does not change the list of team members shown. All linked team members will still be displayed, regardless of location.
This can be surprising if you're expecting the filter to control the displayed values from the relationship itself. It only controls which parent records (in this case, companies) appear in the view.

blocks.text: Editing attributes for records linked via relationships

segments.t: Whether an attribute shown through a relationship attribute can be edited depends on the type of relationship:
If the relationship allows multiple linked records, any fields you show through that relationship will be view-only. You’ll be able to see the values but not update them from the current view.
If the relationship allows only a single linked record, the fields you show can be edited directly from the view.

faq.q: Can I associate multiple companies to a deal?

segments.t: Attio’s system relationship attribute Associated deals <> Associated company only supports one company per deal. To add multiple companies per deal, create a custom relationship attribute.

faq.q: Can I report on historical pipeline data after migrating to Attio from another CRM?

segments.t: It isn’t possible to migrate all historical stage change data. The best approach is to separate views and reports on deals: one for deals created prior to the migration, and another for new deals created in Attio after the migration.

If you still have access to your previous CRM, run and save reports there to preserve a record of your historical pipeline. It’s also recommended to export your historical deal data into a CSV so you can continue to reference it.
When migrating into Attio, you can use a
(for example, a checkbox) to mark migrated deals. This allows you to create two distinct views:
: Filter by the checkbox being checked
: Filter by the checkbox not being checked

During the transition, you will need to work out of both views, and you may want to export data from Attio and combine it with your previous CRM data to create unified reports. Over time, as migrated deals are closed, your view of migrated deals will naturally phase out and become a historical reference, then you’ll reference and report on new deals created in Attio going forward.

faq.q: What happens to reports when records are deleted or removed from lists?

segments.t: Deletion of records or list entries has the following impact on reports:
When records are deleted, reports on the object remove the records’ data on refresh.
When records are removed from a list, reports on that list remove the list entries’ data on refresh.

In both cases, reports stay up to date with the current data in your workspace. If records or list entries are no longer relevant or active but you don't want to lose the historical data, use filters to hide them from views instead of deleting them. That way, the historical data is still available in reports.

title: Set up a Funnel report
description: Measure conversion rates through stages.
desc: Measure conversion rates through stages.

lines.t: Available on plus, pro, enterprise and ultra plans.

segments.t: This article explains how to set up a Funnel report, which shows how records move through stages in a pipeline, helping you measure conversion rates and identify drop-off points.

lines.t: For an overview of all report types and when to use each one, see

segments.t: See Attio Academy for a video walkthrough of Funnel, Time in stage, and Stage changed reports.
Use funnel reports to track conversion rates, drop-off points, and how effectively your pipeline is progressing.
If you want to know how many records are
report instead. Funnel reports measure progress through stages over time, not current counts.

In a funnel report, each percentage shows the conversion rate from one stage to the next. The calculation only considers records that entered at least one of the included stages in your funnel. For each step, it checks how many of those records that reached the previous stage also went on to reach or surpass the current stage.
Number of records that have reached or surpassed the current stage ÷ Number of records that reached or surpassed the previous stage
This ensures each step reflects progression, rather than overall totals across the entire funnel.

Only records that enter at least one of the stages you include in the funnel are included in the calculation. For example, if your Deal stage attribute includes Lead > In progress > Won, but your funnel report only includes Lead and In progress, a record that moved directly from Lead to Won will not be counted.
If a record skips a stage, it’s still counted as having passed through that stage.
If a record moves backward (from a later stage back to an earlier one), it’s still counted as having reached the later stage.
Funnel reports count all records that have
been in the selected stages, not just those still in them.
Follow these steps to set up a Funnel report:
Select an object, list or activity.
Choose a status attribute whose stages define your funnel.

, select which stages to include in the funnel.Include one target stage. This is usually Won when tracking conversion rate, or Lost when analyzing loss. Do not include both Won and Lost in the same funnel.Typically you should remove stages like Churned or Paused.

segments.t: Funnel reports are designed to track progress toward a single target stage. To avoid confusion and inflated counts:
End each funnel at a single outcome stage (e.g. Closed Won, Closed Lost, or Disqualified).

faq.q: Why do the numbers in my funnel report look different than expected?

segments.t: It is common for Funnel reports to show numbers that do not match your pipeline view. This does not mean the report is wrong. Funnel reports measure stage progression differently than other report types.

Funnel reports do not show how many records are currently in a stage. They count how many records have ever reached or moved past that stage. If you want to see the current stage of records, use an Insight report instead.
Records that skip a stage are still counted as having reached it. For example, if a deal moves from Lead to Won without passing through In progress, it will still be counted in In progress.

Records that move backward are still counted at the highest stage they reached. For example, if a deal was once marked Won but later moved back to Negotiation, it will still be counted as having reached Won.
These differences in logic explain why Funnel reports often show higher totals than other reports.

faq.q: How does a Historical values report handle changes within a time period?

segments.t: Historical values reports capture each record’s value at the end of the reporting period. For example, in a report grouped monthly, a deal that started the month in Qualification but ended the month in Won would only count toward Won for that month.
If the current period is still in progress, you’ll see

. The data shown for an incomplete period reflects your records as they are right now and can still change until the period ends. Once the period is complete, the report captures the final values as they were at the end of that time range and those values will no longer update.

For instance, if your weekly report currently shows 215 records in a particular stage and you move one record elsewhere, the count will drop to 214 because the week isn’t finished yet. When the week ends, that total becomes fixed.
If you want to track how records move between stages, use a Time in stage or Stage changed report instead.

faq.q: How does Attio enrich a person record with multiple email addresses?

segments.t: Attio will check all of the email addresses on a person record for available enrichment data and add all data from the emails to the record.

In cases where more then one email address has enrichment available for the same attribute, Attio will enrich the value coming from the primary email address first (the first one listed on the record), then fallback to the second, etc.

faq.q: What information does Attio require in order to enrich a record?

segments.t: Attio's data enrichment requires a domain (e.g
) for companies or an email address for person records. If a company is missing a domain, it can't be enriched - the same goes for a person without an email address.

faq.q: Regarding communication intelligence attributes like ‘connection strength’, whose interactions are used to calculate this data point for companies?

segments.t: Attio will only factor in interactions with people whose email domain (

) when calculating communication intelligence attributes for company records. ⁠ ⁠This means that there is no way currently to factor emails with public email domains (such as Gmail or Outlook) into company communication intelligence data. People you have manually linked to companies will also not factor into the companies' communication intelligence if their domains don't match the companies'.

faq.q: Why isn't Attio enriching an attribute or adding an image to a record?

segments.t: Attio uses enrichment data from third-party providers, which requires an email address for person records and a domain for company records. These identifiers allow Attio to look up and add available details automatically.
However, enrichment isn’t guaranteed. Data coverage can vary depending on the region and market.

If you’ve already added an email address or domain and still don’t see any enriched attributes or images, it means that Attio’s data providers don’t currently have that information available for the record.

segments.t: When you are putting the same record through a process more than once, for example if you have more than one deal or opportunity with the same company, you can add it to a list multiple times. ⁠ ⁠When you go to add a record to a list that is already in the list, you will see the option to select the record already in the list to edit the attribute values for the existing instance, or you can click

faq.q: Why can't I add a record to a specific list?

segments.t: Each list is specific to companies or people. When you open a list, you will see

designated to the right of the list name. ⁠ ⁠If you are trying to add a record to a list but don't see the list as an option, consider whether you are trying to add a person to a companies list or a company to a people list, which won't be possible.

faq.q: Should I choose People or Companies for my new list?

segments.t: When you go to create a list from scratch, ask yourself whether it is mainly data about people or companies that you will be tracking in the list. ⁠ ⁠For example, if you have a "Deal Flow" list, you may want to track things like the number of employees at the company, the company's category, or the company's city. In that case, it's best to use a list of companies rather than a list of people, and you can always pull in your point(s) of contact by adding an attribute column for it. ⁠ ⁠Alternatively, if you have a "Recruiting" list, it probably makes more sense to have a list of people rather than companies. You can also pull in "Company" as an attribute in your list of people.

You will need to identify which records are relevant to your list and add them manually. Unlike object views which are visible to all members of a workspace, it's possible to restrict who can view a list. ⁠ ⁠You can create multiple views within the same list, and all views will hold all records in the list, but you can use filters to show/hide different subsets of records on each view. faq.q: Should I use separate lists or multiple views within a single list?

segments.t: We generally recommend using different lists only when you're going to be working with entirely different sets of records and tracking different data points - for example, one list for recruiting and another list for a sales deal pipeline. Keep in mind that list attributes are only able to be viewed in the list where they're created.
For seeing different subsets of records within a single list, you can create multiple views, and
to narrow down which records are relevant.

For example, you can have a "Recruiting" list with a select attribute for "Role". You can create multiple views, filtering each view using the "Role" attribute to show one role per view. So within your "Recruiting" list, you can have different views for "Marketing specialist", "Customer support specialist", and "Engineering manager", for example. Other list attributes such as "Role level", "Manager", "Stage", and "Potential start date" can be used across all views in the list.

faq.q: Should I use the Deals object or a Sales list of companies for my deal flow pipeline?

segments.t: For simple sales processes, using the Sales list (available as a
) is an easy way to get started. If you're looking for a more robust, scalable solution, we'd recommend using the
for a walkthrough of Deals vs. Sales lists.

The key difference between the Deals object and a Sales list of companies is that a deal record can be your central source of truth for notes, tasks, and attribute values related to that deal. In addition, with deals you can use
to link them to records of other objects like people, companies, etc., and you can
to show the relevant data in a format that makes most sense for your team.

The same cannot be said of entries in a companies list. You can store deal-related information in a company record, but if multiple teams will use companies, that record could become cluttered quickly. A sales person will want to easily see the information that's relevant to them for a specific deal that is in progress, which is easier with Deals, especially if there may be more than one deal in progress with a single company.

segments.t: Rules let you control when changes to records can be saved. Each rule has a condition that determines when it applies and one or more requirements that must be met. If the condition is met but a requirement isn't, Attio blocks the change.
For example, you can require Deal value before a deal moves to Won, or require Lost reason before it moves to Lost.

blocks.text: When a rule blocks a change

segments.t: If a change meets a rule’s condition but doesn’t meet its requirements, Attio blocks the change. When editing a record in Attio, an
dialog opens showing the change that triggered the rule and the attributes that need values.
Fill in the required values, then click

. Attio saves your original change along with the values you added. If a value you enter triggers another rule, the dialog refreshes to show the additional attributes you need to fill in. Closing the dialog without saving discards the change.
Rules apply to any change you make yourself, wherever you make it. That includes the Attio web app, the mobile app, CSV imports, Ask Attio, suggestions, and the Attio MCP.
If a row doesn't meet a rule's requirements, that row isn't imported. It shows as
with the error "Blocked due to object rules violation."
The attributes the rule requires are added to the approval card. Set the values and click
to apply all the changes together, or click
The attributes the rule requires are added to the suggestion. Set the values and click
If a block tries to make a change that a rule blocks, the block fails. Open the run and select the failed block to see the reason. Learn more about

Attio's API, along with many apps in our app marketplace, use tokens to authenticate API requests to Attio. Rules apply to API updates made through user-scoped tokens only. If an API call doesn't meet a rule's requirement, the call will fail. Rules are not applied to API updates made through tokens that are scoped at the workspace level.

Rules don't apply to changes Attio makes on its own. This includes enrichment, email and calendar sync, the interaction attributes Attio maintains such as First interaction and Last interaction, records created automatically from email and calendar activity, and data brought in by Import2. Rules also don’t currently apply to legacy workflows.

blocks.text: Records that already break a rule

segments.t: Creating a rule doesn’t change or flag existing records that don’t meet its requirements.
The next time one of those records is edited, the rule is checked. The change can’t be saved until the record meets the rule’s requirements, even if the attribute being edited isn’t part of the rule.
For example, if Deal value is required when Deal stage is Won, changing the name of an existing won deal with no Deal value prompts you to add Deal value before the change can be saved.

faq.q: What's the difference between a required attribute and a rule?

segments.t: A required attribute must always have a value when a record is created. Required attributes are only supported on custom objects.
A rule makes an attribute required only when specific conditions are met. For example, you can require Deal value only when Deal stage is Won. Rules can be created for any object.

faq.q: Can I use a rule to stop a record from being deleted?

segments.t: No, rules apply to attribute values when a record is created or updated.

faq.q: What are the differences between Attio's People and Users objects?

segments.t: are a complete library of every human (usually represented by an email address) that your company has interacted with. Most person records are created automatically through Attio's email and calendar sync, which creates people for anyone you've ever emailed or had a calendar event with. Customers also create people records when they receive leads (e.g. via an inbound form or when purchasing a lead list), create users records (see below), or import data from other communication tools beyond email.

is useful for tracking information about the users of a product, including the person and workspace records they are connected to. It includes the following attributes: ID, Primary email address, Person, Workspace, List Entries, and Next due task. Common custom User attributes include product-usage information like User type (e.g. admin vs standard user), status (active/inactive), and usage history (e.g. number of log ins in the last 30 days). When creating a user record, we recommend linking it to a person record (and creating the person record if necessary) so that you can tie together your communication history available on the person record to the user information available on the user record.
Additionally, there are differences in functionality available for People and Users:

faq.q: Should I use the Deals object or a Sales list of companies for my deal flow pipeline?

segments.t: For simple sales processes, using the Sales list (available as a
) is an easy way to get started. If you're looking for a more robust, scalable solution, we'd recommend using the
for a walkthrough of Deals vs. Sales lists.

The key difference between the Deals object and a Sales list of companies is that a deal record can be your central source of truth for notes, tasks, and attribute values related to that deal. In addition, with deals you can use
to link them to records of other objects like people, companies, etc., and you can
to show the relevant data in a format that makes most sense for your team.

The same cannot be said of entries in a companies list. You can store deal-related information in a company record, but if multiple teams will use companies, that record could become cluttered quickly. A sales person will want to easily see the information that's relevant to them for a specific deal that is in progress, which is easier with Deals, especially if there may be more than one deal in progress with a single company.

Email sources determine which emails appear on an Emails tab. Adjusting these sources helps ensure relevant conversations appear on the right records, even when they don’t follow default domain-based rules.

By default, a company’s Emails tab only shows emails where the sender or recipient’s domain matches the company’s domain. This means emails sent from personal or secondary work addresses can be missed.
Adding Team > Email addresses as a source on Companies ensures that emails sent or received by anyone added to the Team attribute appear on the company’s Emails tab, regardless of email domain.

For example, if you have a custom Events object with an Event attendees relationship to people, you can add an Emails tab that uses Event attendees > Email addresses as a source. This surfaces all emails involving event attendees directly on the event record.

segments.t: You can add more than one Emails tab to the same object, each with different sources. This is useful when you want to separate different types of communication instead of showing everything in a single tab.
For example, on Deals you might:
Keep the default Emails tab showing all emails related to the associated company.
Add a second Legal emails tab that uses the Legal POC
and selects the Email addresses attribute on that related person.

With this setup, the main Emails tab shows general deal communication, while the Legal emails tab only shows emails involving the legal point of contact. This makes it easier to focus on specific conversations without filtering through unrelated emails.

blocks.text: What happens when I merge two records?

segments.t: When merging records you combine all data including list entries, notes, folders and files, tasks, comments, and call recordings and meetings from two source records into a single record. Emails will also be merged when two person records are merged.

Merging creates a new record rather than keeping one of the two originals. Both source records are marked as merged, and the record you end up with has a new record ID (and URL) that is different from either of the records that went into the merge.

The data for the record on the right is prioritized, so its values take precedence where the two records hold conflicting data. You can swap the order of records by clicking the arrow icon between them.

blocks.text: Admit, deny, or stop recordings during meetings

segments.t: , you'll be prompted to admit or deny the Attio call recorder at the start of each external meeting. Admit Attio to record the call or deny it to prevent the call from being recorded.

lines.t: If you join a meeting early, Attio’s call recorder will enter the waiting room 30 seconds before the scheduled start time. If not admitted within 10 minutes, it will automatically leave the waiting room.Keep in mind, if you've just created and joined a new calendar event, the call recorder may take a few minutes to join as the event syncs with Attio.

segments.t: If you've admitted Attio, you can remove it at any time to stop the recording by following the platform-specific instructions below or by asking Attio to leave directly in the meeting chat.
For example, any participant can send any of the following messages in the chat to remove Attio from the call and stop recording on Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams:
You can only ask Attio to leave after it has been admitted to the call.

You must always adhere to the relevant data privacy laws of the participants of a meeting. For example, you may need to obtain consent from all participants before recording a call. It is your responsibility to ensure relevant laws are followed when using this feature, but the following guidelines may be helpful:
Notify participants before the call that you intend to record it, for example by including this in the meeting invite.
Update relevant privacy notices to include call recording.
Before admitting the Attio call recorder into your meeting, ask all participants for verbal consent to the recording of the call and make a note of this.
If any participant does not consent, either leave the call recorder in the waiting room (preventing the recording) or deny it entry.

If a participant withdraws consent during a recorded call, remove the Attio call recorder to stop the recording. The recorded portion will remain accessible in Attio from the time the recorder was admitted until it was removed.

blocks.text: What is a support access request?

segments.t: A support access request is used to grant an Attio employee temporary access to your Attio workspace to resolve an issue or technical problem. Requests can be approved or denied by workspace admins.

blocks.text: When does a support access request occur? Can I initiate one myself?

segments.t: Most support issues can be quickly resolved via

, but sometimes further investigation is needed. Our team will discuss the process with you before requesting access, usually once a chat or email support issue is escalated. Support access requests are always initiated on the side of an Attio employee rather than an Attio user.

blocks.text: How do I approve a support access request?

segments.t: If you are a workspace admin, you can approve or deny support requests. In the sidebar, click on the dropdown beside your workspace name and choose
. Here you’ll see new requests with their current status, as well as a history of any prior requests. Select

blocks.label: The Support Requests section of Attio's Workspace settings. In this example, a request to remotely access the account is pending, with an Accept and Deny button beside it.
blocks.alt: The Support Requests section of Attio's Workspace settings. In this example, a request to remotely access the account is pending, with an Accept and Deny button beside it.

blocks.text: What access does a support request grant? Is my data secure?

segments.t: Once accepted, a support request temporarily grants the Attio employee full admin access to your workspace. All Attio administrators undergo background checks and are routinely trained on security practices. Access is also audited independently by a third party as part of our compliance program to ensure your data is secure.

blocks.text: How long will you have access to my workspace?

segments.t: Support access is usually limited to seven days.

description: Manage your billing information and payments.

segments.t: If you're a workspace admin, you can manage payment and plan details for your Attio workspace.

Each Attio workspace is billed separately, and you’ll be billed according to your plan, the number of seats in your workspace, and any add-ons. If you belong to multiple workspaces, your seat is counted and charged separately for each one.

Billing intervals are either monthly or annual, and set per workspace. Annual billing offers a discount compared to monthly billing. You'll always be billed at the start of your billing interval. You can pay in USD, GBP, or EUR.

New Attio workspaces start with a 14-day free trial of the Pro plan. During the trial, your team has access to all Pro features. When the trial ends, workspace admins can choose to continue on any plan including the Free plan.

Your workspace is billed per seat. A seat is a paid spot in your workspace that can be occupied by one active member or pending invite at a time. For example, if you’ve purchased 10 seats, you can have up to 10 members or invites in your workspace.

You can suspend or replace members as needed, but billing is tied to the number of seats, not how many people are actively using them. Suspending a member frees their seat for a new member, regardless of whether you choose to retain their email and calendar data.

If you need to invite more people than your current seat count allows, you’ll need to add seats first. If you’ve reduced your team size and have unused seats, you can remove seats to avoid being billed for them in future cycles.

If you retain their email and calendar data:
Their synced emails and calendar events remain in Attio. Workspace members can request access to these emails through the email access handler you assigned.
Communication intelligence data from their synced accounts remains visible. Suspended members are clearly identified as suspended in communication intelligence views.

faq.q: Do integrations use workspace credits?

segments.t: Integrations only use workspace credits if they are part of a workflow (for example, when
) or if they trigger an existing workflow when making updates.

faq.q: Do sequences use workspace credits?

segments.t: Emails sent directly from sequences don’t use workspace credits. Credits are only consumed when sequences are part of a workflow automation. For example, using the Enroll in sequence block to add people automatically will use credits each time that workflow runs.

faq.q: Do record summaries use credits?

segments.t: No. Record summaries are included on all paid plans and don't use workspace or seat credits.

faq.q: What happens when I run out of seat credits for Ask Attio?

segments.t: When you run out of seat credits, your usage of Ask Attio continues with workspace credits (unless your admin has disabled this setting). If workspace credits are disabled or you've reached the workspace credit limit for Ask Attio, you won't be able to use Ask Attio until your credits renew.

faq.q: Can I share my seat credits with other workspace members?

segments.t: No. Seat credits are personal to each member and can only be used for Ask Attio. They cannot be transferred or shared with other workspace members.

faq.q: When do my seat credits renew?

segments.t: Seat credits renew monthly on your billing date, along with workspace credits.

title: Export audit logs
description: Export a record of changes made in your workspace.
desc: Export a record of changes made in your workspace.

lines.t: Available on enterprise and ultra plans.

segments.t: The audit log is a record of what changed in your workspace, who changed it, and when. Use it to give auditors evidence of who changed what, to investigate a record that was deleted or overwritten, or to review a member's activity before they leave your team. Admins export the log as a CSV file for a date and time range, and can filter it by actor and type of change.
The audit log records changes to records and attributes. Records include tasks and list entries.
Each entry includes details such as:
The workspace member who made the change
When the change happened, shown in UTC
What changed, such as a record, task, or list entry, and which attribute
The IP address and country the change came from

The audit log doesn't currently include record views, sign-ins, admin actions such as changes to members or permissions, changes to notes or workflows, or workspace configuration changes. Only changes made by workspace members are included currently, not changes made with workflows, the API, etc.
Attio keeps audit logs for one year. Logs older than that are deleted.

lines.t: Logging starts on the date audit logging is turned on for your workspace. Changes made before that date aren't in the audit log.

How Attio and your IDP work together

lines.t: Available on enterprise and ultra plans.

segments.t: SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) lets you manage Attio workspace membership directly from your identity provider (IDP). Adding someone in your IDP provisions them in Attio, and removing them suspends their access.
. You can use either feature without the other, though many organizations use both together.
First, make sure you have at least one
on your workspace. This is the best way to use SCIM, and allows you to add users directly to your workspace. Without a verified domain, you will only be able to send workspace invites to those users.

blocks.text: Linking an Attio workspace with an identity provider

segments.t: For step-by-step instructions on configuring your identity provider, see:
Set up SCIM with Microsoft Entra
When a new user is provisioned via SCIM, Attio uses an available seat on your subscription first. If no seats are available, the provisioning request fails.
Click your workspace name and select
When enabled, Attio will use an available seat if one exists, or automatically add a new paid seat to your subscription if not.
Once SCIM is configured, your IDP controls how members are provisioned and managed in Attio.

Assigning a user to the Attio SCIM integration in your IDP adds them to your workspace. If a user with that email already exists in Attio, they are linked to the workspace rather than provisioned as a new user.
Users are provisioned as non-admin members by default. To provision someone as an admin, set their role to
in your IDP before assigning them.
How a user is added depends on their email domain:
The user is added to the workspace directly and receives an email notifying them they've been added. New Attio users also receive a welcome email.
The user receives a workspace invite and is added once they accept it.
Removing or deactivating a user in your IDP suspends their Attio workspace membership immediately and revokes their session.
It’s not possible to delete or downgrade the last remaining admin in a workspace. First, give another member admin access.
Set and update roles using the
attribute in your IDP. Attio supports two roles:
. An unrecognized role value defaults to member. If both roles are assigned to the same user, admin takes precedence.
SCIM groups map to Attio teams. Pushing a group from your IDP to Attio creates a new team, or you can link an IDP group to an existing team.

blocks.text: How Attio and your IDP work together

segments.t: Your IDP is the source of truth for any members and teams provisioned through it. If a change is made directly in Attio, such as updating a role or team membership, your IDP will reconcile it back to its own state on the next sync.
Any members or teams not currently managed by your IDP can still be managed freely from within Attio and won't be affected by syncs.
To stop syncing, remove your credentials from your identity provider. If you connected using a developer token, you can also delete it from
. Once the token is removed, your IDP can no longer provision or suspend members in Attio.
All changes made via SCIM remain in place and are not reverted.

faq.q: What happens to a member's data when they are suspended via SCIM?

segments.t: Suspending a member via SCIM has the same effect as manually suspending them in Attio. See
how suspending a member impacts data

faq.q: Can I use SCIM across multiple verified domains?

segments.t: on your workspace. When a user is provisioned, Attio checks all verified domains to determine whether to add them directly to the workspace or send them an invite.

faq.q: Can I use SCIM without a verified domain?

segments.t: Yes. If your workspace doesn't have a verified domain, or if a user's email doesn't match one, they will receive a workspace invite rather than being added directly. They become active workspace members once they accept the invite.

faq.q: How can I configure SSO for multiple workspaces with the same domain?

segments.t: You only need to set up SSO once. In Attio, users log in to the app itself rather than to a specific workspace. Once SSO is configured for your domain, any user with that domain can log in and access all of the workspaces they’re a member of.

This means you don’t have to configure SSO separately for each workspace. The login method is determined by the user’s email domain, so a single setup ensures that SSO works across all workspaces under that domain.
If someone is a member of multiple workspaces using the same domain, logging in with SSO will take them first to the workspace where SSO was set up. From there, they can
manually switch to any of their other workspaces

faq.q: How do I change my Attio email address if my workspace uses SSO?

segments.t: The way this works depends on whether the new email uses the same domain as the one currently associated with your account.

SSO in Attio is enforced at the domain level, not the individual email address. If your workspace has SSO enabled for examplecorp.com, any email ending in @examplecorp.com will continue to log in via SSO. Changing your email from alex.jones@examplecorp.com to alex.smith@examplecorp.com, for example, does not require any changes to your SSO setup and you can update the email directly in Attio.

If you change your email to a different domain, such as alex.jones@samplemail.com, SSO will no longer apply because the new domain is not verified for SSO in the workspace. In that case, you will need to sign in using email and password unless the new domain is added and verified for SSO.

faq.q: Can I enable SSO for one domain but not another?

segments.t: Yes. SSO applies only to the domains you've verified, so verify the domains you want it to cover and leave the others unverified.
Users on a verified domain sign in through your identity provider, or with Google if
is disabled. Users on any other domain can sign in with a temporary password or with Google, and
If you verify both domains on the same workspace, SSO applies to both. There's no way to verify a domain and then exclude it from SSO. Learn more about

faq.q: What happens if the email access handler is suspended?

segments.t: If a workspace member who handles email access requests for a suspended member is themselves suspended, you'll be prompted to assign a new handler before completing their suspension.

faq.q: What happens to retained email data if a suspended member is reactivated?

segments.t: Retained mailbox data remains visible in Attio, and any emails that were shared while the member was suspended remain shared. Once the member is reactivated, their mailbox goes back to being a normal synced mailbox that they manage themselves, and admin retention controls no longer apply.
